results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 46 aligned units' outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their spec paragraphs, in spec order (sections, unit counts and forms also match per structure.json).

results.draft_locus: Introduction ¶2
results.finding: Outliner flagged two ideas (invoice persists / Stripe vs Adyen retry units). Spec p02's controlling idea deliberately joins both: the invoice and that its holder decides what a provider can recover. Intended.

results.draft_locus: Questions to Ask ¶2
results.finding: Outliner flagged two ideas (answer to opening puzzle / hand-off). The spec requires both the conclusion callback (to the 4 April question) and the hand-off (p46) at the end of the conclusion; the paragraph joins them through the frozen tax invoice. Intended.

Every body unit traces to C1-C5: invoice section to C1 (incl. p13 e-invoicing as a tax reason for the immutable record), attempts and cash application to C2/C4, declines to C3, recovery-figure and public-record paragraphs to C5, designs/comparison/Larkfield/failures to C2-C4.

results.draft_locus: Can Another Attempt Succeed? Decline Type and Payment Method ¶2
results.quote: A fixed schedule picks the days in advance. Stripe's custom schedule allows “up to three retries, each with a specific number of days after the previous attempt”, and Orb, a billing system, says in its documentation (n.d., accessed November 2026) that it retries “after 1, 4, and 9 days from the initial payment attempt”. The alternative is learned timing.
results.finding: The fixed-schedule examples are followed directly by 'The alternative is learned timing' with no sentence saying what they show. The spec's point (a fixed schedule is blind to the reason for the decline and to the cardholder's pay cycle) never appears, so the reader is not told why learned timing is an alternative worth having.

All other evidence is explained: state table (p09: 'The row to notice is the third'), Figures 1-4 by captions, finalization and tax quotations (p10), credit-note example (p11), void/uncollectible quote (p12), ViDA (p13 closing sentence), vendor recovery figures (p16), requirements table, hard-decline quote, Visa limits, account updater quotes, direct-debit quotes, customer-message evidence, bank-transfer and reconciliation facts, Auto Rescue quote ('“Smart” and “optimal” are Adyen's words'), Orb, trade-off table, public-record facts with inference block, comparison table (read in p33), Larkfield policy and curve tables, and the three failure cases.

results.draft_locus: Attempts Against a Debt: Why the Invoice Outlives Its Payments ¶3; Who Runs the Collection: Three Designs ¶5; Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ table; Sources
results.quote: I found no independent, dated measurement of the share of churn that is involuntary, so this chapter quotes none; its argument needs none.
results.finding: Every recovery figure is attributed: Stripe's 55% and US$8.2bn (product page, marketing), Adyen/Pinterest 4% (Adyen knowledge hub), Adyen's 6% (2020 post), Larkfield's 50% labeled illustrative. No churn share is quoted, and the absence of an independent measurement is stated in p16 and the Sources section.
